title: Personalized, intuitive & visual QT-prolongation monitoring using patient-specific QTc threshold with pseudo-coloring and explainable AI.
authors: Alahmadi, Alaa; Davies, Alan; Vigo, Markel; Jay, Caroline
one_liner_zh: 该文研究药物诱导QT间期延长的心电监测与可解释AI可视化，完全不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或转录因子结合，与课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Drug-induced QT-prolongation increases the risk of TdP arrhythmia attacks and sudden cardiac death. However, measuring the QT-interval and determining a precise cut-off QT/QTc value that could put a patient at risk of TdP is challenging and influenced by many factors including female sex, drug-free baseline, age, genetic predisposition, and bradycardia. OBJECTIVES: This paper presents a novel approach for intuitively and visually monitoring QT-prolongation showing a potential risk of TdP, which can be adjusted according to patient-specific risk factors, using a pseudo-coloring technique and explainable artificial intelligence (AI). METHODS: We extended the development and evaluation of an explainable AI-based technique- visualized using pseudo-color on the ECG signal, thus intuitively 'explaining' how its decision was made -to detect QT-prolongation showing a potential risk of TdP according to a cut-off personalized QTc value (using Bazett's ∆QTc > 60 ms relative to drug-free baseline and Bazett's QTc > 500 ms as examples), and validated its performance using a large number of ECGs (n = 5050), acquired from a clinical trial assessing the effects of four known QT-prolonging drugs versus placebo on healthy subjects. We compared this new personalized approach to our previous study that used a more general approach using the QT-nomogram. RESULTS AND CONCLUSIONS: The explainable AI-based algorithm can accurately detect QT-prolongation when adjusted to a personalized patient-specific cut-off QTc value showing a potential risk of TdP. Using ∆QTc > 60 ms relative to drug-free baseline and QTc > 500 ms as examples, the algorithm yielded a sensitivity of 0.95 and 0.79, and a specificity of 0.95 and 0.98, respectively. We found that adjusting pseudo-coloring according to Bazett's ∆QTc > 60 ms relative to a drug-free baseline personalized to each patient provides better sensitivity than using Bazett's QTc > 500 ms, which could underestimate a potentially clinically significant QT-prolongation with bradycardia.
abstract_zh: 背景：药物诱导的QT间期延长会增加TdP心律失常发作和心源性猝死的风险。然而，测量QT间期并确定一个精确的QT/QTc截断值以判断患者是否存在TdP风险，具有挑战性，且受多种因素影响，包括女性性别、无药物基线、年龄、遗传易感性和心动过缓。目的：本文提出了一种新颖的方法，用于直观和可视化地监测QT间期延长，显示潜在的TdP风险，可根据患者特异性风险因素进行调整，采用伪彩色技术和可解释人工智能（AI）。方法：我们扩展了一种基于可解释AI技术的开发和评估——该技术通过ECG信号上的伪彩色进行可视化，从而直观地“解释”其决策是如何做出的——用于根据个性化QTc截断值（以Bazett's ∆QTc > 60 ms相对于无药物基线和Bazett's QTc > 500 ms为例）检测显示潜在TdP风险的QT间期延长，并使用从一项评估四种已知QT延长药物与安慰剂对健康受试者影响的临床试验中获取的大量ECG（n = 5050）验证其性能。我们将这种新的个性化方法与之前使用更通用方法（使用QT-nomogram）的研究进行了比较。结果与结论：基于可解释AI的算法在调整到个性化患者特异性QTc截断值以显示潜在TdP风险时，能够准确检测QT间期延长。以∆QTc > 60 ms相对于无药物基线和QTc > 500 ms为例，算法分别产生了0.95和0.79的灵敏度，以及0.95和0.98的特异性。我们发现，根据每位患者个性化的无药物基线，使用Bazett's ∆QTc > 60 ms调整伪彩色，比使用Bazett's QTc > 500 ms提供更好的灵敏度，后者可能低估伴有心动过缓的潜在临床显著QT间期延长。
